review_topics: EASIX across CKM stages before clinical CVD
discovery_layer.scientific_role: Examines a three-laboratory composite in relation to linked long-term all-cause and cardiovascular mortality, with complex-survey modeling, dose-response analysis and stage-specific observations.
discovery_layer.evidence_position: Retrospective analysis of prospectively collected survey data and linked deaths; adjusted associations and descriptive discrimination, with main-text sensitivity summaries.
citation_contexts: Methods: distinguish raw counts, weighted estimates, exposure scale and adjustment models in NHANES survival analysis.
Discussion: routine-lab risk markers in CKM stages 0-3 and the evidence needed beyond an adjusted mortality association.

display_title: EASIX and long-term mortality in CKM stages 0-3: a survey-weighted NHANES analysis
summary: Among 10,885 NHANES adults at cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) stages 0–3, higher baseline endothelial activation and stress index (EASIX) was associated with all-cause and cardiovascular mortality. The study describes the associations across CKM stages and compares the index with its individual laboratory components.
research_question: Is baseline EASIX associated with long-term all-cause and cardiovascular mortality among adults at CKM stages 0-3, and how do those associations vary by exposure shape, CKM group and analytic adjustment?
author_summary: The study links NHANES 1999–2018 data for 10,885 adults aged at least 30 years to mortality through 31 December 2019. Over a median 97 months, there were 1,122 deaths, including 295 cardiovascular deaths. In survey-weighted Model 2, each raw EASIX unit was associated with an all-cause mortality HR of 1.41 (95% CI 1.24–1.61) and a cardiovascular mortality HR of 1.30 (1.13–1.49). The highest versus lowest sample quartile HRs were 1.55 (1.22–1.96) and 2.51 (1.54–4.07), respectively. The estimated cardiovascular association was steeper at lower values. EASIX generally had numerically higher discrimination than its individual components earlier in follow-up, whereas creatinine had higher AUCs at the longest times. Full-cohort interactions across CKM stages did not reach statistical significance. Positive associations were also reported after lifestyle and eGFR adjustment and in an age-restricted analysis.

study_profile.study_design: Retrospective analysis of prospectively collected NHANES 1999-2018 baseline data linked to mortality through 2019; complete-case primary survey-weighted Cox analysis with spline, subgroup and sensitivity analyses.
study_profile.evidence_type: Population-based observational mortality association; descriptive time-dependent discrimination against individual laboratory components.
study_profile.population: US civilian noninstitutionalized adults aged ≥30 years with valid fasting-subsample weight, baseline CKM stages 0-3, EASIX components, linked mortality and complete primary covariates. CKM stage 4 excluded.
study_profile.primary_endpoint: The two mortality outcomes were all-cause and cardiovascular death, tracked from the baseline examination to death or 31 December 2019. Cardiovascular death used the linked underlying-cause classification.
study_profile.secondary_endpoint: Additional analyses characterized the shape, discrimination and CKM-group estimates for the same two mortality outcomes.
data_modalities: Survey demographics, medical history and examination
LDH, creatinine, platelet count and metabolic/renal laboratory measures

cohorts.name: Analytic NHANES CKM cohort
cohorts.role: Complete-case primary analytic participants; CKM stages 0–3, aged ≥30 years

study_profile.counting_note: The cohort total, EASIX quartile sizes and death counts are unweighted. CKM stages 0–1, 2 and 3 comprise 2,898, 6,751 and 1,236 of the same participants, with survey-weighted proportions of 31.19%, 61.95% and 6.86%. Table 1 uses survey-weighted means and percentages, and sample medians and ranges for EASIX.

key_findings.claim: The analytic cohort links baseline CKM measurements with long-term mortality in adults without reported clinical CVD.
key_findings.context: Ten NHANES cycles, complete-case selection and public-use mortality linkage.

evidence.label: Analytic sample
evidence.value: 10,885 adults aged at least 30 years at CKM stages 0–3. The study excluded stage 4.

evidence.label: Selection
evidence.value: Of 11,922 otherwise eligible participants, 1,037 (8.70%) were excluded for missing primary covariates. Counts of missing values for individual variables overlap.

evidence.label: Follow-up
evidence.value: Follow-up from the baseline mobile examination to death or 31 December 2019. Median follow-up was 97 months.

evidence.label: Outcome counts
evidence.value: 1,122 all-cause deaths, including 295 cardiovascular deaths

evidence.label: Baseline summaries
evidence.value: The weighted mean age was 50.63 years (SE 0.20). Women numbered 5,608 and represented 52.32% after survey weighting.

key_findings.source_locator: Methods 2.1, Study Design and Population. Figure 1 caption. Results 3.1 and Table 1.

key_findings.claim: EASIX and the CKM-stage assignment are explicitly defined from baseline survey measurements.
key_findings.context: A routine-laboratory composite and retrospectively operationalized CKM classification.

evidence.label: Index formula
evidence.value: EASIX = lactate dehydrogenase (U/L) × creatinine (mg/dL) ÷ platelet count (10⁹/L). Each component was measured once at the baseline mobile examination.

evidence.label: Exposure scale
evidence.value: Cox models use one raw EASIX unit for continuous estimates and Q1 as the reference for quartile comparisons.

evidence.label: Quartile boundaries
evidence.value: Sample quartile boundaries were 0.340, 0.457 and 0.616. The observed range was 0.024–11.542.

evidence.label: CKM definition
evidence.value: The study assigned the highest qualifying stage under the 2023 AHA framework. Stage 3 was operationalized as very-high-risk CKD or a 10-year PREVENT base total-CVD risk of at least 20%. Stage 4 used self-reported clinical CVD and was excluded.

evidence.label: Older-age handling
evidence.value: The primary PREVENT calculation assigned age 79 to those aged 80 or older. The separate age-restricted analysis covers ages 30–79.

key_findings.source_locator: Methods 2.1–2.3. Table 1 (EASIX range). Discussion (PREVENT age range).

key_findings.claim: The primary estimates use fasting-subsample survey design and stated adjustment sets.

evidence.label: Design
evidence.value: Combined fasting-subsample weights, SDMVSTRA sampling strata and SDMVPSU primary sampling units

evidence.label: Estimator
evidence.value: Survey-weighted Cox models used svycoxph with design-based linearization variance. The quartile trend test assigned each quartile its median EASIX.

evidence.label: Model 1
evidence.value: Age group (under 60 or at least 60 years), sex, race and ethnicity, marital status, education and family poverty-income ratio

evidence.label: Model 2
evidence.value: Model 1 plus current smoking, body mass index, systolic blood pressure, fasting plasma glucose and antihypertensive, glucose-lowering and statin use

evidence.label: Reporting units
evidence.value: Table 1 presents weighted means with standard errors for continuous variables, unweighted counts with weighted percentages for categorical variables, and sample medians, interquartile ranges and ranges for EASIX.

key_findings.claim: Higher EASIX is associated with mortality in the primary adjusted Cox summaries.
key_findings.context: Survey-weighted Cox Model 2 estimates for the two mortality outcomes.

evidence.label: Lower quartiles
evidence.value: The all-cause Q2 and Q3 confidence intervals included 1. The cardiovascular Q2 HR was 1.58 (95% CI 0.93–2.68), P = 0.093.

evidence.label: Across adjustment sets
evidence.value: In crude, Model 1 and Model 2 analyses, the continuous HRs were 1.59, 1.43 and 1.41 for all-cause mortality and 1.57, 1.34 and 1.30 for cardiovascular mortality. Quartile trend P values were below 0.001 for both outcomes across all three models.

key_findings.claim: The cardiovascular mortality association rose more steeply at lower EASIX values.
key_findings.context: Spline estimates and descriptive comparisons of the three laboratory components.

evidence.label: Spline design
evidence.value: The 10th, 50th and 90th percentile knots were 0.26, 0.46 and 0.83. EASIX 0.46 was the reference at HR 1.0.

evidence.label: All-cause shape
evidence.value: P for nonlinearity = 0.466

evidence.label: Cardiovascular shape
evidence.value: P for nonlinearity = 0.008. The main text describes a steeper increase at lower EASIX and a more gradual increase later, with wider confidence intervals at high values.

evidence.label: Discrimination
evidence.value: The study compared time-dependent AUCs for EASIX, LDH, creatinine and platelets at 12–240 months. EASIX generally had numerically higher AUCs earlier in follow-up. Creatinine had higher AUCs at the longest times.

evidence.label: Evidence role
evidence.value: The AUC comparisons were descriptive. The main text does not report exact AUC values.

key_findings.source_locator: Methods 2.5 (splines and AUC). Results 3.2–3.3. Figures 2–3 captions.

key_findings.claim: Mortality estimates varied numerically across CKM stages. Full-cohort interaction P values were 0.062 and 0.057.
key_findings.context: Model 2 stratum estimates per one EASIX unit, with stages 0 and 1 combined.

evidence.label: CKM strata
evidence.value: Stages 0–1 included 2,898 participants, stage 2 included 6,751 and stage 3 included 1,236. These are unweighted counts.

evidence.label: All-cause HRs by stage
evidence.value: For stages 0–1, 2 and 3, respectively, HRs were 2.14 (95% CI 1.45–3.16), 1.28 (1.06–1.56) and 1.41 (1.27–1.57). Interaction P = 0.062.

evidence.label: Cardiovascular HRs by stage
evidence.value: For stages 0–1, 2 and 3, respectively, HRs were 2.63 (95% CI 1.34–5.16), 1.27 (1.03–1.57) and 1.01 (0.78–1.31). Interaction P = 0.057.

evidence.label: Precision
evidence.value: The combined stages 0–1 group had 17 cardiovascular deaths. The stage 3 cardiovascular estimate was close to the null.

evidence.label: Age-restricted finding
evidence.value: In ages 30–79, all-cause interaction P was 0.047 and cardiovascular interaction P was 0.068. The authors describe the age-restricted all-cause finding as exploratory.

key_findings.source_locator: Methods 2.5 (subgroup design). Results 3.1 and 3.4. Figure 4 caption. Discussion (CKM-stage estimates and 17 early-stage cardiovascular deaths).

key_findings.claim: The authors report positive associations in several sensitivity analyses, including after additional lifestyle and renal adjustment.
key_findings.context: Sensitivity results reported in the article’s main text.

evidence.label: Early deaths/imputation
evidence.value: The main Results reports positive associations after excluding deaths within two years and after multiple imputation of missing covariates, with details cited in Tables S2 and S3.

evidence.label: Lifestyle subset
evidence.value: Alcohol, sleep duration and HEI-2015 were added. All models were refitted in the same complete-case subset. HRs were 1.66 (95% CI 1.38–1.99) for all-cause and 1.43 (1.08–1.91) for cardiovascular mortality. The main text gives no subset size.

evidence.label: eGFR sensitivity
evidence.value: Adding eGFR categorized at 90 mL/min/1.73 m² gave HRs of 1.40 (95% CI 1.23–1.59) for all-cause and 1.24 (1.08–1.43) for cardiovascular mortality.

evidence.label: Age restriction
evidence.value: Excluding 549 participants aged at least 80 years left 10,336. Model 2 HRs were 1.41 (95% CI 1.23–1.62) for all-cause and 1.33 (1.14–1.55) for cardiovascular mortality.

evidence.label: Competing event
evidence.value: The article describes Fine–Gray and cumulative incidence analyses treating noncardiovascular death as a competing event. Cumulative cardiovascular death incidence was highest in Q4.

evidence.label: Ages 30–79, stage-specific all-cause mortality
evidence.value: For CKM stages 0–1, 2 and 3, the main text gives HRs of 2.10 (95% CI 1.40–3.15), 1.28 (1.05–1.56) and 1.39 (1.23–1.57), respectively. Interaction P = 0.047.

evidence.label: Ages 30–79, stage-specific cardiovascular mortality
evidence.value: For those same stages, the main text gives HRs of 2.48 (95% CI 1.23–4.97), 1.29 (1.05–1.58) and 1.00 (0.75–1.34), respectively. Interaction P = 0.068.

key_findings.source_locator: Methods 2.5 (sensitivity analysis). Results 3.4. Discussion (renal, stage and lifestyle paragraphs).

what_this_adds: Extends EASIX research to linked long-term mortality across CKM stages 0-3, using a readily computed three-laboratory index.
Provides survey-weighted continuous/quartile estimates and complementary shape, component and CKM-group analyses for risk-marker comparison.
Examines several adjustment/selection sensitivities while identifying renal overlap and the further evidence needed to establish clinical value.

supports: Observed adjusted associations of baseline EASIX with linked all-cause and cardiovascular deaths in the selected NHANES cohort.
The reported spline shape, descriptive marker-discrimination comparisons and stage-specific estimates with their interaction/precision limits.
Main-text sensitivity summaries under additional adjustment, missing-data and age/competing-event analyses.
does_not_establish: A specific endothelial mechanism or a causal effect of EASIX.
Incremental prediction over an established risk model, a clinical threshold or improved decisions and outcomes.
Applicability to CKM stage 4, younger adults, institutionalized populations or populations outside the United States.

qa.question: Who was analyzed and how long were outcomes tracked?
qa.answer: The primary cohort included 10,885 NHANES 1999–2018 participants aged at least 30 years at CKM stages 0–3. Mortality follow-up extended to 31 December 2019. Median follow-up was 97 months, with 1,122 deaths, including 295 cardiovascular deaths.

qa.question: How is EASIX calculated and scaled in the models?
qa.answer: EASIX is LDH (U/L) × creatinine (mg/dL) ÷ platelet count (10⁹/L). The components were measured at the baseline examination. Continuous HRs are per one raw unit. Sample-quartile boundaries were 0.340, 0.457 and 0.616.

qa.question: How were CKM stages and older ages handled?
qa.answer: The researchers assigned the highest qualifying stage using the 2023 AHA framework. Stage 3 used very-high-risk CKD or a 10-year PREVENT base total-CVD risk of at least 20%. Stage 4 used self-reported clinical CVD and was excluded. Participants aged 80 or older were assigned 79 for the primary PREVENT calculation. A sensitivity analysis restricted ages to 30–79.

qa.question: Which weights and covariates define the primary models?
qa.answer: The Cox models used combined fasting-subsample weights, strata, sampling units and design-based linearization variance. Model 1 included age group (under 60 or at least 60 years), sex, race and ethnicity, marital status, education and poverty-income ratio. Model 2 added current smoking, body mass index, systolic blood pressure, fasting glucose and antihypertensive, glucose-lowering and statin use.

qa.question: What mortality associations are reported in Table 2?
qa.answer: Model 2 gives per-unit HRs of 1.41 (95% CI 1.24–1.61) for all-cause and 1.30 (1.13–1.49) for cardiovascular mortality. The highest versus lowest quartile HRs were 1.55 (1.22–1.96) and 2.51 (1.54–4.07), respectively.

qa.question: What did the splines and AUC comparisons show?
qa.answer: The nonlinearity P value was 0.466 for all-cause and 0.008 for cardiovascular mortality. The text describes a steeper cardiovascular association at lower EASIX. EASIX generally had higher AUCs than its individual components early and midway in follow-up, while creatinine had higher AUCs at the longest times. These were descriptive comparisons.

qa.question: How did the mortality estimates vary across CKM groups?
qa.answer: In the full cohort, interaction P values were 0.062 for all-cause and 0.057 for cardiovascular mortality. The cardiovascular HR in stage 3 was 1.01 (95% CI 0.78–1.31), and stages 0–1 had 17 cardiovascular deaths. For ages 30–79 the P values were 0.047 and 0.068, respectively. The authors treat the age-restricted all-cause subgroup pattern as exploratory.

qa.question: What did additional adjustment and age restriction show?
qa.answer: After adjusting for alcohol, sleep and diet quality in a common complete-case subset, the HRs were 1.66 (95% CI 1.38–1.99) for all-cause and 1.43 (1.08–1.91) for cardiovascular mortality. With additional eGFR adjustment they were 1.40 (1.23–1.59) and 1.24 (1.08–1.43). The positive associations also persisted at ages 30–79. Renal function contributes to both EASIX and CKM staging, which limits attribution to a specific endothelial mechanism.

data_types: Routine LDH, creatinine and platelet count

limitations: EASIX is a single baseline measurement combining LDH, creatinine and platelets. Residual confounding, including physical activity, and shared creatinine in EASIX and renal staging limit a specific endothelial interpretation.

The primary analysis excluded 1,037 otherwise eligible participants for missing covariates. Misclassification is possible for survey-derived CKM stages, self-reported clinical disease and cause-of-death coding.
Participants aged 80 or older were assigned age 79 for PREVENT. The age-restricted sensitivity analysis does not verify those older individual stage assignments.

Exact AUC points and subgroup values reported only in figures were unavailable for this summary. Supplemental Tables S1–S7 and Figure S1 were also unavailable. This limits verification of supplemental covariate distributions, full sensitivity tables and the competing-risk curve. The primary article reports the estimates cited above.
